### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/architecture.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/events.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/anatomy.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5493b8842995fabb0979ae535301d3f3cb9fc65e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8e94c1e9445ceabe4313bc6f75b83008f7fe8547` — the merge of head `08182e92e841af25746ca51776c4847728033dac` into base `5493b8842995fabb0979ae535301d3f3cb9fc65e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8e94c1e9445ceabe4313bc6f75b83008f7fe8547 && git checkout 8e94c1e9445ceabe4313bc6f75b83008f7fe8547
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5493b8842995fabb0979ae535301d3f3cb9fc65e 08182e92e841af25746ca51776c4847728033dac && git checkout -B drift-repro 5493b8842995fabb0979ae535301d3f3cb9fc65e && git merge --no-ff 08182e92e841af25746ca51776c4847728033dac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5493b8842995fabb0979ae535301d3f3cb9fc65e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5493b8842995fabb0979ae535301d3f3cb9fc65e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `525f355ce2b02f8877ae5d405b85347a4949a079`
Local-runs: none

PR #28755 (card #28713), reviewed 2026-11-01T17:38Z against merge-base `1c5b1773` with `origin/main`. Face: the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone (`record-recognisers --paths` finds no schema, governed or narrowing hit on the eight changed paths; the changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides the declaration face, whose tier is `TIER_DEFAULT`). The review itself was run at the contract tier on the seat's instruction; the tier a face sets is not a ceiling. Inputs: the diff, the card and its four comments (triage 6559633664, claim 6560597942, amendment 6560860207, os-dev-report 6561408622), the PR body, the head's check-runs, the order and the seat's two later conditions.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@objectstack/core` gains one public member, `dispatchesBootPhaseHooks(): boolean`, on `ObjectKernelBase` (so `LiteKernel`) and on `ObjectKernel`.** Right. It is read-only (no setter, no state written; `ObjectKernel` reads a construction-time option), documented on both classes with the same contract, and correct on both kernels: `ObjectKernelBase` answers `true`, and `LiteKernel.bootstrap()` dispatches `kernel:ready`, `kernel:bootstrapped`, `kernel:listening` unconditionally after every `start()`; `ObjectKernel` answers `config.bootPhaseHooks !== false`, and its `bootstrap()` returns before the three hooks exactly when `bootPhaseHooks === false`. The method name follows the option it reports. Reachable from a plugin through `PluginContext.getKernel()` (typed `ObjectKernel`), which is how the automation service and the three kernel tests read it. Additive: no signature, export or accepted value of either package changes; no consumer break. The spec package's `api-surface` covers `@objectstack/spec` only, so no baseline moves. No `content/docs` page names `bootPhaseHooks`, so no prose falls out of date.
- **`@objectstack/service-automation`: stored entries deferred to the `kernel:bootstrapped` pass, conditionally.** Right. `start()` sets `holdStoredEntries` from `kernelDispatchesBootPhaseHooks(ctx)` once, just before the boot reconcile; the reader answers `false` when `getKernel` is absent or throws, when the member is absent or not a function, or when it answers anything but `true`. While held, `reconcileDeclaredConnectors` skips an entry only when PR #28671's unchanged classifier says `why === 'stored'` and records `storedEntriesHeld`; host-declared and installed entries take the start pass as before. The existing #28591 `kernel:bootstrapped` pass (`fatal: false`) clears the hold inside the serialized reconcile queue and runs the reconcile when anything was held even on an unchanged fingerprint. Because the hold is cleared only there, the `metadata:reloaded` reconcile and the degraded-retry timer cannot serve a stored entry early. On a kernel that answers `false`, and on a host that does not expose the member, the hold is never set and stored entries keep today's start pass: a stored connector is never left unserved (seat condition 1), pinned by three unit cases (a real `ObjectKernel` with `bootPhaseHooks: false`; a `LiteKernel` with the reader removed; one answering `false`) and by ablation 2 reddening exactly those three.
- **Outcome for a stored row under a plugin connector's name.** Right. The connector plugin registers in its own `start()` (connector-slack declares `dependencies: ['com.objectstack.service-automation']`), so by the bootstrapped pass the plugin holds the name; the reconcile's existing ADR-0097 §4 check (`!existing && getConnectorOrigin(name) === 'plugin'`) reports through the one `fail(msg, cause, stored)` reporter from PR #28729, which in soft mode logs the same record and skips. No second skip path is added; the §4 text, the plugin-wins precedence and `assertSameOriginOrFree` are untouched, so no §4 ruling is needed. Pinned by the unit case (origin `plugin`, the plugin's action resolves, the stored one does not, the record present) and by the restart dogfood (second start finishes, the plugin's `slack` lists `ready` with the plugin's actions, the boot record names the stored entry).
- **Controls.** Right. A stored entry under a free name is absent when a later plugin starts and present at `kernel:listening` (unit), and `ready` on the first read after the restart (dogfood): the moment it becomes ready is pinned. PR #28729's `#28698` stored-fault describe is unchanged and, on `LiteKernel`, now exercises the deferred pass: green. The host's own entry under a plugin connector's name still fails the boot (unit control); #28534's `installed` / `unrecorded` readings are not touched.
- **Order rulings.** All held: same verdict as the running platform; no precedence change; no save-door refusal (named as a follow-up); host-declared entries unchanged.
- **Availability class.** The PR body, commits and changeset state the outcome in product words and carry no recipe. The restart dogfood and the unit describe carry the measurement, which is where the order puts it; the card body was already public.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28713-stored-connector-plugin-name-at-start.md`: `@objectstack/service-automation: patch`, `@objectstack/core: patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the PR body line for line. **Consistent and correct.** The level axis (AGENTS.md, maintainer ruling A on #25105; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) grades by the metadata protocol alone: a `none` declaration must grade every introduced entry `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". A new read-only kernel method is a public-surface widening and no change to what a metadata author can write, so `yes (widening)` + `none` + `patch` is the honest pair; the `minor` the claim amendment named for core would have been refused by that gate. The declaration pair is right, not the level.
- The `Check Changeset` check-run on this head concluded `success`; the dev also ran the gate with the PR body as event, exit 0.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Dev deviation "Clause-② measured `yes (widening)`, not the order's expected `no`": accepted; the measurement is right (see ①) and the order said to declare what is measured.
- Dev deviation "core changeset `patch`, not the amendment's `minor`": accepted (see ②); the amendment's level was not per the rule.
- Out-of-scope finding "save-door refusal for a stored connector under a host plugin connector's name": with the seat as a possible follow-up; a narrowing, correctly left out of this PR per the order.
- **Residue (seat condition 2), stated in product words in the PR's Acceptance notes, first bullet:** saved connectors become available a little later during the start (about a third of a second on the showcase), still before the server accepts requests; an automation that runs during the start itself (a record change made by the app's own start-up work, or a scheduled job whose first run falls inside the start) and calls a saved connector would find it not yet available; measured on an instrumented showcase restart as not observed. Honestly stated; the second bullet also says the fix does not apply on a kernel that withholds its boot-phase hooks or a host that does not say. Nothing else observable during start changes for host-declared or installed connectors.
- Overlap: open PR #28693 edits `service-automation/src/plugin.ts` in one hunk near line 4971 (flow precedence), far from this pass; `git merge-tree` of this head with its head is clean.
- CI state at 2026-11-01T17:38Z: on head `525f355c`, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates and Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests are `success`; Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, the remaining Lint and Type Check jobs are `in_progress`; none failed. The merge-base `1c5b1773` carries no non-green check-run over its 131 runs, so no red can be excused by signature. Landing waits for the full set green (precondition ②), which is the seat's read at queue time.
- Not measured locally: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (dev: prerequisite not met in the checkout); CI's Build Core covers it.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay author note owed.
- No must-fix. Not required for landing, for the seat's judgment: the PR is still a draft and carries no `needs:contract-review` label; nothing in the record changes that.
